gap: No result ChatGPT got puts these together: a stock Synology DS225+ ships with exactly 2 GB, Synology's VMM rule says VMs run only on a NAS with more than 2 GB, and Home Assistant says an HAOS VM needs at least 2 GB. So the DS225+ cannot run an HAOS VM until a RAM module is added, even though its spec sheet lists '2 recommended VM instances'. On a 2 GB DS220+, VMM offered the auto-generated VM only 272 MB.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Synology VMM 7.4 spec page, the cited QNAP USB 3.2 Gen 1 FAQ and terabytewise.com, which ChatGPT got but did not cite. Synology's VMM page states the 'more than 2 GB' rule but names no model. Terabytewise says the DS225+ ships with 2 GB and that 'that minimum is all the memory they have', but it never cites the VMM floor or the 272 MB a 2 GB unit leaves for a VM. The QNAP FAQ covers only guest-OS USB 3 support. It does not mention QNAP's 4 GB minimum for Virtualization Station or its advice to keep VMs at or below 50% of RAM. No rival lays out each maker's RAM floor and USB passthrough wording side by side, but the key DS225+ conclusion can be pieced together from two of them.
decides: It rules out a stock DS225+ for an HAOS VM, so 'DS225+ / DS925+' on our page should become 'DS925+, or a DS225+ only with an added 4 GB module'. The DS925+ (4 GB ECC, 8 recommended VM instances) and the QNAP TS-264 (8 GB, where Virtualization Station needs at least 4 GB and QNAP advises giving VMs at most 50% of memory, leaving about 4 GB for HAOS) both clear the 2 GB HAOS minimum out of the box. On USB, all three main makers pass through a single device rather than a whole port or controller, so USB support doesn't separate them. On QNAP the only USB-speed caveat is guest-OS USB 3 support, which HAOS's Linux kernel meets, and the TS-264 also has USB 2.0 ports. UGREEN's DH2300 and DH4300 Plus cannot run VMs at all, so only the DXP models qualify.

findings.label: Minimum resources for an HAOS VM
findings.value: 2 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs, UEFI boot; the KVM image is .qcow2, VirtualBox .vdi, VMware .vmdk
findings.note: The page lists 'Memory: 2 GB of RAM' and 'Processors: 2 vCPUs' under minimum resources and says 'Home Assistant requires UEFI to boot'. It describes a 32 GB default disk only in the Unraid steps. For KVM, USB dongles are passed with --hostdev busID.deviceId, i.e. per device.

findings.label: Host RAM floor, file system and USB passthrough type for Virtual Machine Manager
findings.value: VMs run only on a NAS with more than 2 GB of memory; VM data only on Btrfs volumes; USB 2.0/3.0 passthrough; at least one CPU thread reserved for the host; UEFI or Legacy BIOS boot
findings.source_title: Virtual Machine Manager Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: Quoted: 'Virtual machines can run only on Synology NAS devices with more than 2 GB of memory.' USB passthrough is listed as unsupported only for Virtual DSM, not for ordinary VMs. The page gives no USB device count.

findings.label: Fitted RAM against the VMM floor
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC fitted, 6 GB max (2 GB + 4 GB), 1 slot; spec sheet lists 2 recommended VM instances
findings.note: The 2 GB fitted is not 'more than 2 GB', so a stock unit falls below VMM's floor and below HAOS's own 2 GB VM minimum. The '2 recommended VM instances' line is footnoted: 'The specifications vary depending on system configuration and memory size.' CPU: Celeron J4125, 4C/4T. USB: 2× USB 3.2 Gen 1.

findings.product: Synology DS220+ (2 GB sibling, used as evidence for DS225+ behaviour)
findings.label: RAM VMM left for an HAOS VM on a 2 GB unit
findings.source_title: RAM blocking HA Supervisor installation on Synology NAS virtual machine - Home Assistant Community
findings.note: From user Bettina's post on 2023-01-01: a DS220+ with 2 GB got 'only 272 MB with 1 CPU'. With less RAM assigned the VM booted but got no IP address. Protoncek replied that Synology officially supports adding a 4 GB stick, for 6 GB total. This is a different model with the same 2 GB configuration and VMM, so treat it as indicative for the DS225+.

findings.label: Fitted RAM and VM headroom
findings.value: 4 GB DDR4 ECC fitted, 32 GB max (16 GB × 2); 8 recommended VM instances; 2× USB 3.2 Gen 1
findings.note: CPU: AMD Ryzen V1500B, 4C/8T, 2.2 GHz. Giving HAOS its 2 GB minimum leaves 2 GB for DSM; this is arithmetic, not a Synology figure. The DS925neo+ has the same layout with non-ECC memory.

findings.label: Host RAM floor and VM memory cap
findings.value: x86 NAS with 4 GB RAM, QTS 4.3.4+ or QuTS hero h4.5.0+; QNAP recommends limiting virtualization apps to at most 50% of memory; USB passthrough unsupported for VMs under the beta High Availability feature
findings.note: The 50% advice sits next to the line 'ZFS uses 50% of the host memory for the ARC by default', so it is aimed at QuTS hero. The USB passthrough exclusion applies only to the beta HA (two-NAS failover) feature, not to standalone VMs.

findings.label: USB passthrough type and guest-OS condition
findings.value: USB 3.2 Gen 1 (5 Gbps) passthrough depends on the guest OS (Linux kernel 3.4.6+); otherwise plug the device into a host USB 2.0 port
findings.source_title: Does Virtualization Station support USB 3.2 Gen 1 passthrough? | QNAP (US)
findings.note: Last modified 2024-07-10. HAOS runs a recent Linux kernel, so it meets the kernel 3.4.6+ condition. Zigbee coordinators are USB full-speed devices, so the USB 2.0 fallback costs them nothing; that last point is my inference, not QNAP's.

findings.label: RAM, USB ports and VM note
findings.value: 8 GB DDR4 fitted, 16 GB max (2 × SODIMM); 2× USB 2.0 + 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A; Virtualization Station note 'At least 4 GB RAM is required'; 4 suggested VM instances
findings.note: CPU: Celeron N5095, 4C/4T. Under QNAP's 50%-of-memory advice, 8 GB leaves 4 GB for VMs, enough for HAOS at 2–4 GB (my arithmetic). The USB 2.0 ports are the ones QNAP's FAQ points to as the fallback.

findings.label: VM support
findings.value: Virtual machines unavailable on DH2300 and DH4300 Plus; VMs are a DXP-series feature
findings.source_title: How to Host VMs on UGREEN NAS
findings.note: Quoted: 'It is unavailable on the DH2300 and DH4300 Plus.' The page date reads 12/01/2026, which is 12 January 2026 in day/month format. The guide gives no minimum RAM and does not say whether USB or PCIe passthrough is supported. A troubleshooting line about 'a USB device already assigned to another VM' implies devices are assigned one per VM. Import formats: IMG, VMDK, QCOW2, VDI; ISO/ISO.GZ; OVA.

findings.label: How a USB stick reaches the HAOS VM
findings.value: Enable the USB controller in the VM's advanced settings, then add the stick under 'USB devices' (per device, not per port); HAOS given 2 vCPU / 4 GB of the 8 GB DDR5; UEFI required
findings.source_title: Home Assistant on a UGREEN NAS – VM Guide | raspberry.tips
findings.note: Article dated 2026-10-21, UGOS Pro (updated 1.7 to 1.12), HAOS 18.2 qcow2. The author says Zigbee stick passthrough is the next article, so this guide does not test a stick. Default MacVTap bridge mode cut the VM off from the NAS; the author switched to a Linux bridge.

findings.product: Synology (VMM) with Home Assistant Connect ZBT-2
findings.label: Known first-setup failure on virtualised HAOS
findings.value: Firmware install step fails ('Failed to flash firmware'); device drops from the VM until detached and reattached; issue open since 2026-02-03
findings.source_title: ZBT-2 first-time installation fails during recommended setup procedure on virtualised HAOS · Issue #162157
findings.note: Reported on an RS1221+ and a DS923+ running VMM, and on a non-Synology host on 2026-07-18. Workarounds from users: reboot the VM from VMM rather than from the HA UI, or flash the firmware on a desktop first. No maintainer reply. ChatGPT's results already include this (rank 25, not cited), so it adds nothing new.

unsourced: UGREEN KB articles 642 (USB device passthrough) and 911 (hardware passthrough): both pages render in JavaScript, WebFetch returned only the heading '知识中心' and running curl needed approval I didn't have, so UGREEN's own wording on device vs whole-port passthrough and its UGOS version scope is left out.
